name: Pricing and SOW construction
oneliner: Scope decomposition, commercial structure, assumptions, change control, and a contract shape that survives procurement.
metaDescription: We construct the commercial side of must-win deals: scope decomposition, pricing structure, assumptions and exclusions, change control, and the SOW draft.

scenarios.title: Procurement wants it line by line
scenarios.text: The buyer loves the solution. Procurement wants every line unbundled, benchmarked, and cut, and your structure was never built to survive that.

scenarios.title: Scope written in a hurry
scenarios.text: The SOW was drafted at midnight before submission. Every ambiguity in it now belongs to your delivery team.

scenarios.title: Change without control
scenarios.text: Six months in, the project is doing work nobody priced, and there is no clause anyone can point at.

what: We construct the commercial side of the deal: decompose the scope, structure the pricing, write the assumptions and exclusions, define change control, and shape the SOW so that what was sold is what gets delivered.
You set the price level and the margin. We build the structure that defends them.

deliverables.name: Scope decomposition
deliverables.desc: The work broken into priceable units, so nothing is sold as a vague whole.

deliverables.name: Commercial structure options
deliverables.desc: Two or three pricing models for this deal, with the trade-offs stated honestly.

deliverables.name: Assumptions and exclusions register
deliverables.desc: Written for a reader with a checklist, because that is who reads it.

deliverables.name: Change control clause set
deliverables.desc: The mechanism that keeps unpriced work from becoming free work.

deliverables.name: SOW draft
deliverables.desc: The full statement of work, ready for your counsel's review.

steps.title: Bring the deal
steps.text: We read the solution shape and whatever scope exists, and tell you where it will leak.
steps.need: The solution outline and draft scope

steps.title: Decompose
steps.text: The work becomes priceable units with owners and boundaries.
steps.need: An hour with the delivery lead

steps.title: Structure
steps.text: We build the pricing model options and pressure test each against how this buyer procures.
steps.need: Your pricing authority in the room

steps.title: Draft the SOW
steps.text: Scope, assumptions, exclusions, and change control, written in plain contract-ready language.

steps.title: Defend
steps.text: Material for the procurement rounds: what moves, what does not, and what each concession costs.

excludes: We do not set your price level or your margin. Those are your calls.
We do not give legal advice. The SOW draft goes to your counsel before it goes anywhere.
We do not negotiate with your buyer. We arm the people who do.
We do not invent benchmarks. Where market data is not available, we say so.

shape.v: A review pass on an SOW you already drafted

domains.name: IT services
domains.note: Rate cards, onshore-offshore mix, and service levels are where services deals get cut. Structure decides margin.

domains.name: B2B SaaS
domains.note: Subscription, implementation, and success services price differently. Bundling them wrong invites the unbundle.

domains.name: BFSI
domains.note: Procurement runs on precedent and audit. Assumptions must be written for a reader with a checklist.

domains.name: Healthcare
domains.note: Long cycles and committee sign-offs mean change control matters more than the day-one price.

related.name: RFP and RFI response
related.desc: The response commits you commercially. This service makes sure it commits you on purpose.

related.name: Security questionnaires and vendor assessments
related.desc: Security commitments flow into the contract. Both documents must agree.

related.name: Proposal deck building
related.desc: The commercial story the deck tells, backed by a structure that holds.
